To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a large number of studies elicited utility values in age-related macular disease (AMD) but that those applied to decision-making have focused on a small number of these.
health state utilities are a major source in economic evaluations of age-related macular disease interventions.
health state utility values are important for decision making in AMD and there is a large body of literature that has elicited values for this condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of utility values for economic evaluations in age-related macular disease (AMD).
the use of health state utility values in decision-making for age-related maculopathy (AMD) and other eye diseases.
the measurement and valuation in health economics of health states, such as those associated with AMD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no one best utility measure to use for decision making in the field of AMD.
the evidence is insufficient to recommend any one set of utility values.
the choice of utility value should be informed by a review of the literature and a consideration of the applicability of the values to the decision problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
utility values for AMD are available and have been applied to decision making.

the choice of utility value is important and should be made on a case by case basis, taking into account the characteristics of the intervention, the patient population, the health state, and the purpose of the utility value.
the literature is still evolving and that the use of utilities in economic evaluations of AMD is likely to continue to evolve as the evidence base for utility measurement grows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of utility values in healthcare decision making is increasing, and the quality of the methods for deriving utility values is improving.
there is an urgent need for the development of a new AMD-specific HRQoL measure, and that this should be a priority for researchers in the field.
utility values are an important component of economic evaluations, and there is a need for more studies to derive utility values and methods to derive them.
